description: Move the presentation the two connectivity views share into connectivityView.tsx and add the one pure geometry helper the drawer needs, leaving the Cloud Map page rendering identically. Precondition for FEAT-002, which consumes both. Covers plan.md items 1-6.
steps: Reset the stale verdict first: overwrite .agents/tasks/connectivity-tab/review.json with {"verdict": "CHANGES_REQUESTED", "findings": [], "note": "reset for the Cloud Map-style redesign; the previous APPROVED verdict belonged to the tab's original build"}. That file is this workflow's stop condition and currently holds the previous task's APPROVED.

Add `compactConnectivityFlow` and its `CompactFlow` interface to the 'Edge geometry' section of frontend-app/src/components/CloudMap/Connectivity/connectivityFlowModel.ts, changing no existing export. Signature and semantics are spelled out in plan.md item 2: args { peers: PeerFlowNode[]; hidden: number; focusW?, focusH?, peerW?, peerH? } defaulting to CFLOW.RESOURCE_W/RESOURCE_H and CFLOW.PEER_W/PEER_H; peers keep model order and fields, get x = focusW + CFLOW.COL_GAP and y re-stacked at a peerH + CFLOW.ROW_GAP pitch from 0; a MoreRow of CFLOW.MORE_H follows the last peer after one ROW_GAP when hidden > 0; the focus sits at x 0 vertically centred on that stack with no negative y (shift the stack down instead, the single-shift normalisation buildConnectivityFlow already ends with); trunkX = trunkFor(focusW); width = focusW + COL_GAP + peerW, or focusW alone when there are no peers and nothing hidden; height = the lower of the focus bottom and the last row's bottom. Comment WHY: buildConnectivityFlow centres a six-column canvas, so the real 18-peer focus sits ~560px down an ~1,120px stack, and this view draws a subset whose rows must close up.

Unit-test it in frontend-app/src/components/CloudMap/__tests__/connectivityFlowModel.test.ts in a new describe after 'buildConnectivityFlow peers', following that file's fixture style (elements -> buildConnectivityIndex -> buildConnectivityFlow -> feed flow.peers in). Cover the two column origins, the pitch, more-row presence/absence and position, the centring, no negative y, width/height, and the empty case.

Append to frontend-app/src/components/CloudMap/Connectivity/connectivityView.tsx, each with its own WHY comment: ACCENT '#4285F4', EDGE_IDLE '#d7dae0', EDGE_LINK '#8b5cf6'; nodeClass(selected) copied character-for-character out of ResourceConnectivityFlow.tsx; peerCardClass({ dashed, confirmed? }) returning the violet peer shell only (confirmed -> emerald border-[1.5px]; dashed -> border-dashed border-[#c4b5fd]; else border-[#ddd6fe]; plus the same rounded-lg bg-white shadow-[0_1px_3px_rgba(0,0,0,0.05)]) and NOT the absolute/layout/size classes, which differ between the views; StateChip verbatim including its good/bad regexes; MoreButton verbatim plus one optional `expanded?: boolean` rendered as aria-expanded; FlowEdge, a single <path> from flowEdge(...) with kind 'contains' (ACCENT 1.8 when selected, else EDGE_IDLE 1.2) or 'connects' (EDGE_LINK 1.5) and an optional dashed flag reproducing today's '4 3' and '3 3' patterns exactly; EdgeLegend({ className }) with the three swatches and the words contains / connects to / inferred.

Update frontend-app/src/components/CloudMap/Connectivity/ResourceConnectivityFlow.tsx to import all of them from './connectivityView' and delete the local copies. Replace each inline <path d={flowEdge(...)}> with <FlowEdge> keeping the same keys, the same parent/child anchor arithmetic and the same kind/selected/dashed; build the peer card's div class list from peerCardClass({ dashed: p.derived || p.external, confirmed: copied === p.id }); replace the legend block with <EdgeLegend className="absolute bottom-2.5 left-3 flex items-center gap-3 text-[10px] text-[rgba(0,0,0,0.45)] bg-white/80 backdrop-blur-sm px-2.5 py-1 rounded-md pointer-events-none" />. Extend the existing comment at the import site to name the newly shared pieces. Change nothing else in the file: the Cloud Map page must be visually unchanged.

Extend the first case in frontend-app/src/components/CloudMap/__tests__/ResourceConnectivityFlow.smoke.test.tsx to assert the legend still names contains, connects to and inferred, and that at least one svg path with a d attribute is rendered. Keep every existing assertion and the 20s timeout comment.

findings:
DONE. npx tsc silent; npx vitest run src/components/CloudMap => 5 files, 38 tests passed. git diff --stat -- frontend-app/src touches only the 3 CloudMap/Connectivity files and the 2 CloudMap/__tests__ files (review.json is untracked in git, so the reset shows as ?? rather than M; pre-existing unrelated M on .agents/tasks/connectivity-tab/design-review.json and xamops-service CloudShellSocketHandler.java were already dirty and were not touched).

connectivityView.tsx now exports, in file order: hoverText, TypeIcon (pre-existing), ACCENT, EDGE_IDLE, EDGE_LINK, nodeClass, peerCardClass, StateChip, MoreButton, FlowEdge, EdgeLegend. It now imports `Icon` from '@iconify/react' (for MoreButton) and `flowEdge` from './connectivityFlowModel' (for FlowEdge) — so connectivityView.tsx depends on connectivityFlowModel.ts, not the reverse; do not import connectivityView from the model.

Exact signatures FEAT-002 consumes:
- compactConnectivityFlow(args: { peers: PeerFlowNode[]; hidden: number; focusW?: number; focusH?: number; peerW?: number; peerH?: number }): CompactFlow, placed in the 'Edge geometry' section immediately after trunkFor.
- interface CompactFlow { focus: Placed; peers: (PeerFlowNode & Placed)[]; more: MoreRow | null; trunkX: number; width: number; height: number }. NOTE: `Placed` is still module-private (not exported) — that is fine for property access (placed.focus.x) and for passing placed.peers around by inference, but FEAT-002 cannot name the `Placed` type in an annotation. If it needs to, export it then; CompactFlow and MoreRow are exported.
- Defaults: focusW/focusH = CFLOW.RESOURCE_W/RESOURCE_H (248/52), peerW/peerH = CFLOW.PEER_W/PEER_H (264/52). peers keep model order and every PeerFlowNode field; x = focusW + CFLOW.COL_GAP, pitch = peerH + CFLOW.ROW_GAP from y 0; `more` ({ hidden, x, y, w: peerW, h: CFLOW.MORE_H }) follows the last peer at the same pitch slot, non-null only when hidden > 0; focus at x 0, y = (stackBottom - focusH) / 2, and when that would be negative the whole stack (peers and more) is shifted down once instead and focus.y = 0; trunkX = trunkFor(focusW) = focusW + 38; width = focusW + COL_GAP + peerW when any row is drawn, else focusW; height = max(last row bottom, focus bottom).

ResourceConnectivityFlow.tsx — nothing beyond the mechanical swap, but two details worth knowing:
(a) the peer card's class list is now ['absolute flex items-center transition-all', peerCardClass({...})].join(' '), so 'rounded-lg bg-white' and the border/shadow come after the layout classes instead of before. Pure Tailwind reordering, no cascade effect, rendering unchanged.
(b) `flowEdge` was dropped from its import list (noUnusedLocals) because every inline <path> is now <FlowEdge>; the import-site comment was extended to name the newly shared pieces. FlowEdge's dash mapping is kind 'connects' => '4 3', kind 'contains' => '3 3', matching what the *More rows drew before.

Smoke test: the first case gained four assertions (getByText for contains / connects to / inferred, and document.querySelectorAll('svg path[d]').length > 0). 'inferred' is unique in that fixture because its single peer is a stated edge; a fixture with a derived peer would also render the card's own 'inferred' badge, so FEAT-002 should use getAllByText there.
